title: Hit the Target
original_question: f(x) = x² - 10. f(a) = 54. Find a. Can there be TWO answers?
core_concept: A quadratic equation can have two distinct real solutions because a parabola is symmetric — the same y-value appears at two different x-values (mirror images across the axis of symmetry). This means the inverse of a parabola is NOT a function unless we restrict the domain, connecting to the concept of non-invertibility and the failure of the one-to-one condition.

easy.question: If f(x) = x² - 10 and f(a) = 54, what equation must a satisfy?
easy.explanation: Step 1: f(a) = a² - 10 = 54. Step 2: This is the equation we need to solve. Step 3: Setting the function equal to 54 and solving for a gives us the input values that produce 54.

easy.question: Solving a² - 10 = 54, what is a²?
easy.explanation: Step 1: a² - 10 = 54. Step 2: Add 10 to both sides: a² = 64. Step 3: The square of a equals 64.

easy.question: If a² = 64, what are the possible values of a?
easy.explanation: Step 1: a² = 64 means a = √64 or a = -√64. Step 2: a = 8 or a = -8. Step 3: Both are valid because squaring either gives 64.

easy.question: Does f(8) = f(-8) for f(x) = x² - 10?
easy.explanation: Step 1: f(8) = 64 - 10 = 54. Step 2: f(-8) = 64 - 10 = 54. Step 3: Both inputs produce the same output — the parabola is symmetric.

easy.question: Why does the equation x² - 10 = 54 have TWO solutions?
options: Because squaring both +8 and -8 gives the same result (64)
easy.correct_option: Because squaring both +8 and -8 gives the same result (64)
easy.explanation: Step 1: 8² = 64 and (-8)² = 64. Step 2: Squaring erases the sign, so both ±8 satisfy a² = 64. Step 3: This is a fundamental property of quadratic equations — they can have two solutions.

easy.question: How many times does the horizontal line y = 54 intersect the parabola y = x² - 10?
easy.explanation: Step 1: The line y = 54 crosses the parabola where x² - 10 = 54. Step 2: x² = 64, so x = ±8. Step 3: Two intersection points means two solutions.

easy.question: Can a linear equation like 3x + 2 = 17 have two solutions?
options: No — a linear equation has at most one solution
Only if the slope is zero
easy.correct_option: No — a linear equation has at most one solution
easy.explanation: Step 1: 3x + 2 = 17 → 3x = 15 → x = 5 (unique). Step 2: Linear equations have a constant slope, so the line crosses any horizontal line at most once. Step 3: Only non-linear equations (like quadratics) can have multiple solutions.

easy.question: What is the axis of symmetry of the parabola y = x² - 10?
easy.explanation: Step 1: The vertex of y = x² - 10 is at (0, -10). Step 2: The axis of symmetry passes through the vertex vertically. Step 3: x = 0 is the axis — points x = 8 and x = -8 are mirror images across it.

easy.question: For f(x) = x² - 10, is f a one-to-one function?
options: No, because f(8) = f(-8) = 54 — two inputs give the same output
every output has exactly one input
Only for positive x — does t match
It depends on the value of 54
easy.correct_option: No, because f(8) = f(-8) = 54 — two inputs give the same output
easy.explanation: Step 1: f(8) = 54 and f(-8) = 54. Step 2: Two different inputs produce the same output. Step 3: This violates the one-to-one (injective) condition, so f is NOT one-to-one.

easy.question: Does f(x) = x² - 10 have an inverse function over all real numbers?
options: No, because f is not one-to-one over all reals
Only for x > 0 — does t match
easy.correct_option: No, because f is not one-to-one over all reals
easy.explanation: Step 1: Since f(8) = f(-8), the function maps two inputs to one output. Step 2: An inverse would need to map 54 back to both 8 and -8, which is not a function. Step 3: Non-one-to-one functions do not have inverses over their full domain.

medium.question: The parabola y = x² - 10 is symmetric. If f(8) = 54, what else must be true?
medium.explanation: Step 1: The parabola is symmetric about x = 0. Step 2: x = 8 and x = -8 are equidistant from the axis of symmetry. Step 3: Symmetric points have the same y-value, so f(-8) = f(8) = 54.

medium.question: How many intersection points does the horizontal line y = k have with y = x² - 10 when k > -10?
options: Depends on the value of k
medium.explanation: Step 1: When k > -10, the horizontal line is above the vertex. Step 2: The parabola opens upward and the line cuts through it. Step 3: A horizontal line above the vertex of an upward-opening parabola always intersects twice.

medium.question: Why is the parabola y = x² - 10 symmetric about the y-axis?
options: Because (-x)² = x², so f(-x) = f(x) for all x
Because the vertex is at the origin
Because the coefficient of x² is 1
medium.correct_option: Because (-x)² = x², so f(-x) = f(x) for all x
medium.explanation: Step 1: f(-x) = (-x)² - 10 = x² - 10 = f(x). Step 2: The function value at x and -x is identical. Step 3: This algebraic identity means the graph mirrors itself across the y-axis — a property of all even functions.

medium.question: Does the parabola y = x² - 10 intersect y = -10?
options: Yes, at exactly one point: the vertex (0, -10)
At two points — does t match
medium.correct_option: Yes, at exactly one point: the vertex (0, -10)
medium.explanation: Step 1: Set x² - 10 = -10. Step 2: x² = 0, so x = 0. Step 3: The only intersection is at the vertex (0, -10) — the horizontal line y = -10 is tangent to the parabola at its minimum.

medium.question: A ball thrown upward reaches height h = 54 metres at two different times. What does having two time values mean physically?
options: The ball is at 54 m twice — once going up, once coming down
The ball is at two different heights at the same time
There is an error in the calculation
medium.correct_option: The ball is at 54 m twice — once going up, once coming down
medium.explanation: Step 1: The parabola of height vs time is symmetric about the peak. Step 2: Any height below the maximum is reached at two different times. Step 3: The ball passes through 54 m on the way up and again on the way down.

medium.question: If f(x) = x² - 10, and we restrict the domain to x ≥ 0, is the restricted function one-to-one?
options: Yes — on x ≥ 0, the function is strictly increasing, so each output comes from exactly one input
Only for x > 10 — does t match
Only if the range is restricted too
medium.correct_option: Yes — on x ≥ 0, the function is strictly increasing, so each output comes from exactly one input
medium.explanation: Step 1: For x ≥ 0, as x increases, x² increases, so f(x) increases. Step 2: Strictly increasing functions never produce the same output twice. Step 3: The restricted function is one-to-one, so it CAN be inverted on this domain.

medium.question: What is the maximum height of the parabola y = -(x-3)² + 20?
medium.explanation: Step 1: y = -(x-3)² + 20 is a downward parabola with vertex at (3, 20). Step 2: The maximum value is 20 when x = 3. Step 3: The negative sign in front of (x-3)² makes the parabola open downward.

medium.question: If a quadratic equation has discriminant b² - 4ac > 0, how many real solutions does it have?
medium.explanation: Step 1: The discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac determines the number of solutions. Step 2: Δ > 0 means the quadratic formula gives two different real values. Step 3: Geometrically, the parabola crosses the horizontal line at two distinct points.

medium.question: The equation x² - 10 = 54 can be rewritten as x² - 64 = 0. Factored, this is:
medium.explanation: Step 1: x² - 64 is a difference of squares. Step 2: a² - b² = (a-b)(a+b), so x² - 64 = (x-8)(x+8). Step 3: Setting each factor to zero gives x = 8 or x = -8.

medium.question: What does it mean geometrically that the parabola y = x² - 10 intersects y = 54 at two points?
options: The horizontal line y = 54 cuts through the parabola at two symmetric locations
The line is tangent to the parabola
medium.correct_option: The horizontal line y = 54 cuts through the parabola at two symmetric locations
medium.explanation: Step 1: y = 54 is a horizontal line above the vertex. Step 2: The upward-opening parabola crosses this line on both sides of the axis of symmetry. Step 3: The two intersection points are mirror images, at x = 8 and x = -8.

hard.question: If f(x) = x² - 10 is not invertible over all reals, but f|_{x≥0} (restricted to x ≥ 0) IS invertible, what is the domain and range of the restricted inverse?
options: Domain: x ≥ -10, Range: x ≥ 0 (inverse maps back to non-negative inputs)
Domain: all reals, Range: all reals
hard.correct_option: Domain: x ≥ -10, Range: x ≥ 0 (inverse maps back to non-negative inputs)
hard.explanation: Step 1: f maps [0, ∞) to [-10, ∞). Step 2: f⁻¹ maps [-10, ∞) back to [0, ∞). Step 3: Domain of f⁻¹ = range of f = [-10, ∞). Range of f⁻¹ = domain of f = [0, ∞).

hard.question: In terms of linear algebra, why does the quadratic f(x) = x² - 10 fail the invertibility test that linear functions like g(x) = 3x + 2 pass?
options: Because f is non-linear (degree 2), so its derivative changes sign, making it non-monotonic — unlike linear functions which are always monotonic
Because f has a negative constant
Because the coefficient of x² is 1
Because f passes through negative values
hard.correct_option: Because f is non-linear (degree 2), so its derivative changes sign, making it non-monotonic — unlike linear functions which are always monotonic
hard.explanation: Step 1: Linear functions with non-zero slope are strictly monotonic (always increasing or always decreasing). Step 2: f(x) = x² - 10 decreases for x < 0 and increases for x > 0 — not monotonic. Step 3: Non-monotonic functions cannot be one-to-one, hence not invertible over their full domain.

hard.question: The fundamental theorem of algebra says a degree-n polynomial has exactly n roots (counting multiplicity, in ℂ). For x² - 64 = 0, how many roots exist?
hard.explanation: Step 1: x² - 64 is degree 2. Step 2: By the fundamental theorem, it has exactly 2 roots in ℂ. Step 3: Both roots (8 and -8) happen to be real, so both appear as x-intercepts of the graph.

hard.question: If we view the equation x² - 64 = 0 as finding the kernel of a non-linear operator, what is the geometric interpretation?
options: The x-intercepts of the parabola — points where the function maps to zero
The axis of symmetry — does t match
hard.correct_option: The x-intercepts of the parabola — points where the function maps to zero
hard.explanation: Step 1: f(x) = 0 means the function maps x to zero. Step 2: These are the roots/zeros of the function. Step 3: Geometrically, they are the x-intercepts — where the parabola crosses the x-axis.

hard.question: For a quadratic y = ax² + bx + c with a > 0, under what condition does the horizontal line y = k intersect the parabola at two points?
options: When k is strictly greater than the minimum value (vertex y-coordinate)
For all values of k — does t match
hard.correct_option: When k is strictly greater than the minimum value (vertex y-coordinate)
hard.explanation: Step 1: The vertex is the minimum point when a > 0. Step 2: A horizontal line above the vertex cuts the upward-opening parabola twice. Step 3: At the vertex height, there's exactly one intersection (tangent). Below the vertex, there are none.

hard.question: If f(x) = x² - 10 and g(x) = x² - 10 restricted to x ≥ 0, what is the relationship between the ranges of f and g?
options: f: ℝ → [-10, ∞) and g: [0,∞) → [-10, ∞) — same range, different domains
f has range — does t match
g has a larger range — does t match
hard.correct_option: f: ℝ → [-10, ∞) and g: [0,∞) → [-10, ∞) — same range, different domains
hard.explanation: Step 1: f takes all real x and produces all values ≥ -10. Step 2: g takes only x ≥ 0 and also produces all values ≥ -10. Step 3: The range is the same [-10, ∞) because the right half of the parabola alone covers all y ≥ -10.

hard.question: The two solutions x = 8 and x = -8 of x² = 64 are symmetric about x = 0. In general, for x² = k (k > 0), the solutions are:
options: x = √k and x = -√k, symmetric about x = 0
x = k and x = -k — does t match
x = k² and x = -k² — does t match
hard.correct_option: x = √k and x = -√k, symmetric about x = 0
hard.explanation: Step 1: x² = k means x = ±√k. Step 2: √k and -√k are equidistant from 0. Step 3: This symmetry about x = 0 is a direct consequence of the even nature of x².

hard.question: In a quadratic regression model y = ax² + bx + c fitting real data, having two x-values for the same y-value means:
options: The model predicts the same outcome at two different input values — a non-unique mapping
hard.correct_option: The model predicts the same outcome at two different input values — a non-unique mapping
hard.explanation: Step 1: If y = ax² + bx + c gives the same y for two x-values, the model is not one-to-one. Step 2: This means knowing the output doesn't uniquely determine the input. Step 3: In practice, this could indicate an optimal input value (vertex) with symmetrical performance on either side.

hard.question: Consider the set V = {f : ℝ → ℝ | f(x) = ax² + bx + c, a,b,c ∈ ℝ}. Is V closed under addition?
options: Yes — the sum of two degree-≤2 polynomials is still degree ≤ 2
— adding two quadratics can give degree 4
Only if both have the same a value
Only for c = 0 — does t match
hard.correct_option: Yes — the sum of two degree-≤2 polynomials is still degree ≤ 2
hard.explanation: Step 1: (a₁x² + b₁x + c₁) + (a₂x² + b₂x + c₂) = (a₁+a₂)x² + (b₁+b₂)x + (c₁+c₂). Step 2: The sum is still degree ≤ 2. Step 3: V is closed under addition (and scalar multiplication), making it a 3-dimensional vector space.

hard.question: Why can't a parabola y = x² - 10 be a level set of a linear function?
options: Because linear functions have straight level sets (lines), not curved parabolas
Because it passes through negative values
hard.correct_option: Because linear functions have straight level sets (lines), not curved parabolas
hard.explanation: Step 1: A linear function f(x,y) = ax + by + c has level sets that are straight lines. Step 2: y = x² - 10 is a curve (parabola), not a straight line. Step 3: Parabolas arise from non-linear (quadratic) functions, not linear ones.

real_life_application.title: Signal Strength at Two Distances
real_life_application.story: A radio signal's strength depends on distance from the transmitter following a quadratic pattern: Signal = d² - 10. Because of the squared term, two different distances (one closer, one farther) can produce the exact same signal strength.
real_life_application.question: Why can two different positions give the same signal strength in this quadratic model?
options: Because the quadratic is symmetric — equal distances from the minimum produce equal outputs
Because radio waves reflect off surfaces
Because the transmitter has two antennas
real_life_application.answer: Because the quadratic is symmetric — equal distances from the minimum produce equal outputs
real_life_application.explanation: Step 1: The quadratic d² - 10 has its minimum at d = 0. Step 2: For any signal value above -10, two distances produce it: d = ±√(S+10). Step 3: The symmetry of x² means equal distances from zero give the same output.

real_life_application.title: Projectile Height (Two Times)
real_life_application.story: When you throw a ball into the air, it reaches any given height twice — once on the way up and once on the way down. The parabola is symmetric, so the same y-value appears at two different x-values (times).
real_life_application.question: When a projectile reaches the same height twice, what does having two solutions tell us about the ball's motion?
options: The ball passes through that height going up, then again coming down
The ball stops at that height
There is an error in the calculation
The ball is at two different heights simultaneously
real_life_application.answer: The ball passes through that height going up, then again coming down
real_life_application.explanation: Step 1: The height parabola is symmetric about the peak time. Step 2: Any height below the maximum is achieved at two different times. Step 3: The two solutions correspond to the upward and downward phases of the trajectory.

real_life_application.title: Profit at Two Production Levels
real_life_application.story: A company's profit follows a downward parabola. At two different production levels (say 20 and 80 units), the profit might be the same. This means the company could produce less and achieve the same profit as producing more.
real_life_application.question: If P(20) = P(80), what does this tell you about the profit function?
options: The profit function is symmetric about x = 50 (the vertex)
The company should always produce 20 units
real_life_application.answer: The profit function is symmetric about x = 50 (the vertex)
real_life_application.explanation: Step 1: P(20) = -400 + 2000 = 1600. Step 2: P(80) = -6400 + 8000 = 1600. Step 3: Both give 1600 — they are symmetric about the vertex at x = 50, where maximum profit occurs.

real_life_application.title: Wave Height at Two Points
real_life_application.story: A cross-section of a wave pool follows the parabolic profile y = 0.5x² - 8. Two swimmers at different positions (x = 4 and x = -4) both stand at the same water depth.
real_life_application.question: At what water depth are both swimmers standing, given they are at x = 4 and x = -4?
real_life_application.explanation: Step 1: y(4) = 0.5(16) - 8 = 0. Step 2: y(-4) = 0.5(16) - 8 = 0. Step 3: Both swimmers are at y = 0, the equilibrium water level, because the parabola is symmetric about x = 0.

real_life_application.title: Arch Design (Parabolic Arch)
real_life_application.story: An architect designs a parabolic arch: y = -x² + 9. The arch touches the ground at two points — these are the two x-intercepts where y = 0. Finding these points is solving -x² + 9 = 0.
real_life_application.question: At what x-coordinates does the arch meet the ground (y = 0)?
real_life_application.explanation: Step 1: Set -x² + 9 = 0. Step 2: x² = 9, so x = ±3. Step 3: The arch spans from x = -3 to x = 3 on the ground, with maximum height 9 at x = 0.
